adapt_rules_reviews_snacs.txt:
Useful SNACS adaptation notes from reviewed examples and guideline headings:

1) Motion verb + destination institution/location with 'to' can take a nonspatial scene role when the endpoint is construed as an organization/institution rather than merely a place.
   - Example: 'Went to the school' -> role p.Org, function p.Goal.
   - Heuristic: with schools/businesses/churches/hospitals etc. after motion verbs, consider p.Org/p.Goal if the destination is institutionally salient.

2) Partitive 'of' after quantifiers/distributives maps item-to-whole.
   - Example: 'Each of you' -> p.QuantityItem/p.Whole.
   - Heuristic: in [quantifier/distributive] + of + NP, role often reflects the selected unit/member and function the larger set/whole.

3) Predicative adjectives of emotion/evaluation can take 'of' introducing the stimulus/topic.
   - Example: 'proud of your massive contributions' -> p.Stimulus/p.Topic.
   - Heuristic: with adjectives like proud, ashamed, aware, etc., 'of' may lexicalize Topic while the scene role is Stimulus.

4) Possessive determiner/genitive is not uniform; distinguish alienable possession from agentive relation.
   - Example: 'your money' -> p.Possessor/p.Possessor.
   - Example: 'your massive contributions' -> p.Agent/p.Gestalt.
   - Heuristic: if possessive marks the doer/originator of a nominalized event/result ('your contributions' = contributions by you), prefer an event-participant construal such as p.Agent/p.Gestalt rather than plain possession.
   - Otherwise with ordinary ownership/control ('your money'), use p.Possessor/p.Possessor.

5) 'throughout' with a calendrical span denotes duration.
   - Example: 'throughout the year' -> p.Duration/p.Duration.

6) 'by' with gerund expressing how speech/action is carried out is Means.
   - Example: 'start out by saying' -> p.Means/p.Means.

7) Business names and street names after 'at'/'on' in service-review text are straightforward locatives.
   - Example: 'at Lovely Nails' -> p.Locus/p.Locus.
   - Example: 'on Military Road' -> p.Locus/p.Locus.

General reminder from guidelines:
- Distinguish scene role vs. lexical function (construal).
- Temporal-locational construals are constrained by the guidelines; avoid inventing such mixed analyses.
- For genitives/possessives, consult special-construction guidance: relations may realize p.Possessor, p.Gestalt, participant roles, etc., depending on the noun semantics.
